The Takeout import finished successfully, but it only added a small amount of data, and it did not connect your API account.

**Completion:** The job succeeded. It processed 9 files and inserted 11 records. Three files were skipped because they aren't in a format the tool reads:
- An HTML file
- A sleep CSV (`sleep_log_entry_id, timestamp, overall_score`)
- A JSON file with an unrecognized structure (top-level key `unknownThing`)

Also, a symbolic link in the archive was not extracted.

**Coverage (local data only):**

| Source | Metric | Dates |
|---|---|---|
| Fitbit Takeout | Steps (2 records) | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit Takeout | Weight (unit unknown, so excluded from summaries) | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit Takeout | BMI | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit Takeout | Heart rate (1 sample) | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit Takeout | Resting heart rate | Oct 1, 2026 |
| Fitbit Takeout | Sleep: minutes asleep, minutes awake, time in bed, efficiency | Oct 2, 2026 (one session) |
| Google Takeout | Steps (1 record) | Oct 3, 2026 |

Every other category has no local records. The data covers only October 1–3, 2026, so it is too thin for trends or summaries.

**Warning:** The resting heart rate file lists one day without an estimate, which was treated as missing. Missing days are not zeros.

**API connection:** No. Importing a Takeout archive only adds local records. It doesn't connect or verify your Fitbit or Google API account. To pull live data, you'd need to connect an account separately, and I can do that if you want.
